messages.subject: Legend bug?
parts:
See below (it's easier than describing :) -- the items in the legend are being attributed to the stat_function layer instead of the size aesthetic. Or, am I missing something?

df <- data.frame(
  x = 1:10, 
  y = 1:10, 
  size = (1:10)/10
)
qplot(x, y, data = df, size = size) +
  stat_function(fun = function(x) x, colour = 'red')

Cheers
david.

messages.author: 45a85351148578ad
messages.subject: RE: Legend bug?
parts:
Hi David,

 

Also complex to explain why, the code bellow worked for me. Think you should specify the size aesthetic for stat_function.

 

library(ggplot2)

df <- data.frame(

  x = 1:10,

  y = 1:10,

  size = (1:10)/10

)

 

qplot(x, y, data = df, size = size) +

stat_function(fun = function(x) x, colour = 'red', size = 0.5, legend = TRUE)

 

# or

 

ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y), data = df) +

                geom_line(aes(stat = stat_function(fun = function(x) x)), colour = "red", size = 0.5, legend = TRUE) +

                geom_point(aes(size = size))

messages.author: e4aec126ff1dca22
messages.subject: Re: Legend bug?
parts: I have received a few emails about my inquiry which lead me to believe a bit of explanation would be helpful.  The point I was trying to bring up is that legends are calculated according to the particular aesthetics used and, in the case of the size aesthetic, seem to be calculated incorrectly.  Notice in the below plots that the plots themselves are always correct, it is just that the legend in the last plot (using the size aesthetic) is generated using the attributes of the stat_function layer as opposed to the geom_point layer.

df <- data.frame(
  x = 1:10,
  y = 1:10,

z = (1:10)/10
)

# using colour aesthetic, no problems
qplot(x, y, data = df, colour = z) +
stat_function(fun = function(x) x, colour = 'red')

# using alpha aesthetic, no problems,
# although now the line appears, curiously  
qplot(x, y, data = df, alpha = z) +
stat_function(fun = function(x) x, colour = 'red')

# using size aesthetic throws the legend off completely 
qplot(x, y, data = df, size = z) +
stat_function(fun = function(x) x, colour = 'red')

Thanks for the comments
david.

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Legend bug?
parts:
Hi David,

This is partly a bug and partly a graph misspecification. The size
aesthetic is inherited by stat_function and even though the geom
correctly ignores it, the legend obviously doesn't. Unfortunately
it's surprisingly hard to cover every edge case and get the legend
displaying correct, especially in cases (like this one) where the
graph specification doesn't really make sense.

Hadley
